html:
SMTO-PSM-0014 — The parameter name has no letters or numbers

GUID: be8a600f-272b-40bd-a574-64762b3fc74c
Slug: parameter-key-empty
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • The name you gave the parameter is made only of spaces or symbols, which SMTO removes, leaving nothing to save it under. The parameter was not saved or renamed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Overview tab in Parameter Store, change Key to a name with letters or numbers, such as prod_server or backup-token. SMTO keeps only letters, numbers, underscores, dots and colons in names, so a name of only symbols becomes empty.
  2. Select Save. Saving with a valid name stores the parameter under the name you'll type after @.
  3. If the Agent was creating the parameter, tell it the exact name to use. The Agent sent a name SMTO couldn't use, and giving it one avoids a guess.

What success looks like

  • The parameter appears in the Parameter Store list under its new name.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Parameter create or rename normalized the supplied key to an empty string (it contained only spaces, punctuation or other unsupported characters).

What this means

  • Parameter creation or rename normalizes the supplied key to an empty value. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Parameter creation or rename normalizes the supplied key to an empty value.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the proposed key after whitespace/normalization, including rename requests.

How to fix it

  • normalize_parameter_key (src/agent_runtime/mentions.py) lowercases the key, turns runs of spaces and dashes into underscores, replaces every other character outside a-z, 0-9, '', '.', ':' with '', collapses repeated underscores and strips leading/trailing '_', '.', ':'. Supply a key that keeps at least one letter or digit after that normalization.
  • Supply a supported nonempty canonical key for creation or rename.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported nonempty canonical key passes normal uniqueness/reserved-name checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
